choices.reason: Dibenzalacetone measured 5.13/10.05 mL at 1/1 and 6.34/20.41 mL at 10/1 (3f6b817d855e67b3b406, 7726f4a207a737256a86). Its 2/1 result tests the revised lower-ratio curve after the prior model's large 1/1 error.
Phenylpyridine measured 15.66/32.11 mL at 10/1 and 28.88/47.57 mL at 20/1 (810b065b0b86ff8c9aae, 434e465cfa7e0034f233). A 5/1 result locates the onset of this rise.

Nitrobenzophenone's measured V2 is 46.72 mL at 10/1, 8.50 mL at 20/1, and 81.30 mL at 50/1 (aef5cafc63ca445e92fa, aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58, b514312eda7950cdcf1c). The 5/1 result probes this unusual condition pattern; its cause is unknown.
Naphthylmethanol at 5/1 measured 24.25/54.11 mL, with V2 21.54 mL above its prior prediction (cdf40bcb3f4392f8d7d1). Its 10/1 prediction of 50.29/94.54 mL tests further alcohol retention growth.

An aromatic secondary alcohol measured 42.23/62.09 mL at 20/1, far later than predicted (2cf4f6424b85ab121943). This related alcohol at 10/1 tests whether late retention extends to another side-chain arrangement; transfer is untested.
The trifluoromethoxy phenol measured 21.85/21.90 mL at 2/1 but 9.58/16.44 mL at 5/1 (4fce6e1a422b4f54c601, 534afc6bd39a8f7923d8). A 1/1 result tests the low-ratio side of this unexpected reversal.
Ethyl nicotinate measured 10.18/20.93 mL at 1/1 and 30.71/60.60 mL at 5/1 (6f827d26c4f82a1bfa90, 855832bd4005ac7abdc6). The 2/1 measurement locates its steep transition.
Dimethylpyridine measured 43.47/118.59 mL at 20/1, far above its prior prediction (51f4126a3aadb3239225). The 10/1 condition tests where that large basic-heteroaromatic response begins.
Nitrobenzaldehyde measured 35.72/98.25 mL at 20/1, with V2 nearly 40 mL above its prior prediction (b85305d91a9e7cfa6005). The 10/1 result tests whether the error persists at a stronger eluent.
Cyanobenzophenone measured 56.47/117.40 mL at 50/1, far above its prior prediction (1395836aef00d6a880b0). A 10/1 result anchors the lower side of its predicted steep high-ratio rise.
Pairing 20/1 with the selected 10/1 cyanobenzophenone and measured 50/1 endpoint tests whether its large retention develops gradually or abruptly. The 20/1 prediction is untested.

A benzyl-substituted β-keto ester at 50/1 was underpredicted in both V1 and V2 (2b97a1e0a6a4b944b760), while a related cyclopropyl ester had a steep ratio response. This simpler acetoacetate tests transfer within the family; evidence is weak.

Salicylaldehyde has a pending 50/1 measurement. Selecting its 0/1 condition gives a broad same-molecule contrast for an aldehyde with a hydrogen-bond donor; no response for this molecule is yet supplied.
Phenylpropanol at 20/1 measured 42.23/62.09 mL against a prior 21.63/33.35 mL prediction (2cf4f6424b85ab121943). Its 10/1 result tests the lower-ratio response of that alcohol.

Cyanobenzophenone's 50/1 response was strongly underpredicted (1395836aef00d6a880b0). This cyanoacetophenone at 10/1 tests whether the combined nitrile–carbonyl motif transfers the error; scaffold and ratio differ, so evidence is weak.

For trifluoromethoxy phenol, the measured 2/1-to-5/1 reversal contradicts a simple eluent-strength trend (4fce6e1a422b4f54c601, 534afc6bd39a8d5ddbf). The 10/1 result tests whether the reversal persists or the response rises again.

hypotheses.content: Several aromatic alcohols measured later than prior predictions at PE-rich conditions, including naphthylmethanol at 5/1, naphthylethanol at 5/1, and phenylpropanol at 20/1. Transfer to different side-chain structures and ratios remains uncertain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected aromatic alcohols remain late at 10/1, and where does their ratio response begin?

hypotheses.content: Basic aromatic nitrogen compounds show steep, molecule-specific PE/EA responses. Nicotinate rises strongly from 1/1 through 10/1, dimethylpyridine was severely underpredicted at 20/1, and phenylpyridine's V2 changes strongly from 20/1 to 50/1. A uniform class correction remains unsupported.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do nicotinate, phenylpyridine, and dimethylpyridine begin their large V1/V2 increases?

hypotheses.content: Para-amino ethyl benzoate measured 10.81/22.83 mL at 2/1 and 26.80/57.07 mL at 5/1, confirming a steep local rise. Aminobenzonitrile similarly measured much later at 5/1 than 1/1, but these different molecules do not establish a common mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the response depend more on amino position, aromatic scaffold, or loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: Enamine ester V2 increases from 16.48 mL at 0/1 to 36.80, 60.45, and 109.68 mL at 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 with DCM loading. A PE-loaded 20/1 result measured 47.00/119.37 mL versus 29.26/109.68 mL for the DCM-loaded record, but V/ul and loading volume also changed.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can a matched loading-condition contrast isolate the source of the 20/1 V1 difference?

hypotheses.content: The cyclopropyl β-keto ester measured 12.33/26.02 mL at 5/1, 19.45/45.11 mL at 10/1, and 44.45/81.20 mL at 20/1. Its response accelerates at weaker eluent, although V/ul differs. Transfer to other β-keto esters remains untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does simpler ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1 also show late elution?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzophenone's recorded V2 is highly nonmonotone across 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1: 46.72, 8.50, and 81.30 mL. The 20/1 measurement contradicts a smooth interval-growth hypothesis. No chemical cause can be inferred from these three records.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 5/1 measurement support the low-ratio trend, and is the 20/1 result isolated?

hypotheses.content: Dibenzalacetone's measured 1/1 result of 5.13/10.05 mL sharply contradicted the prior model's 28.51/66.26 mL prediction. Its 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1 measurements then rise in V1/V2, so the earlier model nonmonotonicity was spurious for the tested points.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 2/1 result fit the measured progression from 1/1 to 10/1?

hypotheses.content: The bromo acid's 1/1 measurement has ordered endpoints, 6.02/9.46 mL, while its earlier 50/1 record has V2 below V1. This supports treating the latter as an anomalous recorded endpoint rather than inferring an elution mechanism from it.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would another high-PE measurement reproduce the impossible endpoint ordering?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzaldehyde at 20/1 and cyanobenzophenone at 50/1 both measured much later in V2 than their prior predictions. Nitroacetophenone at 20/1 also did, but nitrobenzophenone at 20/1 measured early, so a broad nitrile-or-nitro carbonyl rule is unsupported.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At which PE/EA ratios do the selected nitrobenzaldehyde and cyanobenzophenone begin their late V2 response, and does cyanoacetophenone share it?

hypotheses.content: Trifluoromethoxy phenol measured 21.85/21.90 mL at 2/1 but 9.58/16.44 mL at 5/1, reversing the simple eluent-strength expectation for V1. The near-zero 2/1 interval may reflect a special endpoint pattern; its mechanism is unknown.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do 1/1 and 10/1 measurements bracket this reversal or reveal an isolated 2/1 result?

feedback_interpretation: Round-two feedback shifted the search toward specific failures rather than broad functional-group rules. The dibenzalacetone 1/1 prediction was much too late; nitrobenzophenone's 20/1 V2 collapsed between large 10/1 and 50/1 values; aromatic alcohols, nitrobenzaldehyde, and cyanobenzophenone were strongly underpredicted; and the phenol showed an unexpected 2/1-to-5/1 reversal. I selected adjacent condition points and related molecules to test these patterns, while treating the bromo acid's negative interval as an anomalous recorded endpoint.
